# WAVE

> WAVE is a free, open-source digital audio workstation (DAW) for Windows and Linux. It works the FL Studio way (patterns, Channel Rack, piano roll, playlist), includes audio recording and vocal pitch editing, and installs a `wave` command line through which a script or an AI agent can edit the project that is open in the app.

Facts, as of version 0.9 (November 2026):

- Price: free. One build, no paid edition, no account.
- Licence: MIT or Apache-2.0.
- Platforms: Windows (WASAPI, ASIO) and Linux (ALSA and JACK, including PipeWire's JACK; deb, rpm, AppImage). No macOS build.
- Engine: Rust; the audio callback does not allocate, lock or do I/O. Interface: Tauri 2, SolidJS, canvas.
- Built in: a wavetable synth, a sampled grand piano (WAVE Keys), a sampler with a drum and tonal library, and 12 effects (24-band dynamic EQ, compressor, FET compressor, saturator, delay, reverb, limiter, de-esser, denoiser, pitch correction, voice, vocal rider).
- Recording: loop recording with takes and comping, measured latency compensation, live monitoring.
- Vocals: note-level pitch editor, live pitch correction, Tune to Reference, vocal rider.
- Third-party plugins: VST3 effects only, with plugin editor windows on Windows and a parameter list on Linux. No VST instruments, CLAP or LV2.
- Not available: Session view or clip launching, FL Studio project (.flp) import.
- Export: offline bounce to 32-bit float WAV or MP3.
- Made by one developer with AI coding agents.
